QUOTE: "Calls `client.createPost` again. This is a fresh POST, so the server assigns a new post ID." and "On failure, it sets `failed: true` again, unless the error is one of the three terminal errors above, in which case it removes the post."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says retry makes a single fresh createPost call and, on failure, re-marks the post failed or removes it for the three errors. It also notes no automatic retries or loop (retryLimit 0), which covers "no loop or backoff".
